title: Review: Projectile motion; Systems and center of mass; Forces and free-body diagrams; Newton's first law and equilibrium
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 1 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: D02-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; D07-ap1#t4 term and clue written for the game; K04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; D07-ap1#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: D01-1#N.12, D02-1#N.2, D07-1#N.7, D07-ap1#N.2, D01-1#N.14, D02-1#N.11, D07-1#N.9, D07-ap1#N.4, D01-1#N.6b, D02-1#N.4, D07-1#N.2, D07-ap1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Terminal velocity
items.clue: Constant value a skydiver's downward motion settles at once drag equals weight.

items.label: Object model
items.clue: Treatment that ignores the inside, fine when only the motion as a whole matters.

items.label: Time of flight
items.clue: Whole duration in the air: over level ground, twice how long the climb to the top takes.

items.label: Internal forces
items.clue: Pushes and pulls between objects inside the chosen group, adding to zero as third-law pairs.

questions.stem: A crate is given a push and then slides down a rough ramp on its own. Which list gives all the forces acting on the crate while it slides, and no others?

options.text: Weight, normal force, friction up the ramp and a force of motion down the ramp
Weight, normal force and friction down the ramp
Weight, normal force from the ramp and friction up the ramp
Weight, a separate force down the slope, normal force and friction

questions.explanation: Earth pulls down; the ramp pushes perpendicular to its surface and, as the crate slides down it, rubs back up it. Three forces, each with a source.

questions.stem: A space probe is so far from any star or planet that the forces exerted on it are negligible. Its engines fire briefly and then shut off. Which statement describes the probe's motion after the engines have shut off?

options.text: It slows down and stops, as all moving objects do in time.
It slows down as the force from the engine firing is used up.
It moves in a straight line at a constant speed.
It stops almost at once, as no force now pushes it forward.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of mass 2m and length L has a small ball of mass m fixed to one end. How far from the other end of the rod is the centre of mass of the rod–ball system?

Logs burn in an open fireplace. Smoke and hot gases rise up the chimney, and a little ash is left behind. The system is the logs and whatever remains of them in the fireplace. Which statement about the mass of this system is correct?

options.text: It stays constant, since mass is conserved in every physical and chemical change.
It stays constant, since the gases that leave the fireplace have no mass of their own.
It decreases, as the gases produced carry mass across the system's boundary.
It decreases, as the burning destroys the wood's matter and its mass disappears.

questions.stem: A hockey puck is hit by a stick and then slides across level ice. Friction and air resistance are negligible. Which forces are exerted on the puck while it slides, after it has left the stick?

options.text: Earth's pull, the ice's push and a fading push left over from the hit
A downward pull by Earth and an upward push by the ice that touches it
A downward pull by Earth, and no force at all from the ice
An upward push by the ice, with no gravitational force on a supported puck

questions.stem: Which of the following objects is in translational equilibrium?

options.text: A ball at the top of its flight, momentarily at rest
A car rounding a curve on a level road at a constant speed
A puck slowing down on rough ice after a stick stops pushing it
A crate riding up a straight conveyor at a steady 2 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: Its speed and direction are both constant, so its velocity is constant and the net force on it is zero: friction from the belt, up the slope, balances the component of its weight down the slope, and the normal force balances the rest.

questions.stem: A diver makes two dives from the same springboard. In each dive, her center of mass leaves the board from the same height with the same velocity. In dive 1 she keeps her body straight; in dive 2 she pulls into a tight tuck soon after leaving the board. Air resistance is negligible. How do the maximum heights reached by her center of mass in the two dives compare?

options.text: Dive 2's is greater, since pulling into a tuck lifts her body higher.
They cannot be compared, since a rotating object is not a projectile.
They are equal, since her center of mass moves as a projectile in both dives.
Dive 1's is greater, since her outstretched body reaches higher.

questions.stem: A student wants to find the time Earth takes to orbit the Sun once. The student models Earth, with its oceans, its atmosphere and its slowly churning interior, as a single object. Which evaluation of this modeling choice is correct?

options.text: Appropriate: the orbital period depends only on how Earth moves as a whole.
Not appropriate: Earth is much too large to be treated as one single object.
Not appropriate: Earth's oceans, air and interior move relative to one another.
Appropriate: any system can be modeled as a single object, whatever the question.

questions.stem: A rover weighs 1600 N at Earth's surface. Use g = 10 m s⁻². The gravitational field strength at the surface of Mars is 3.7 N kg⁻¹. What is the rover's weight on Mars?
questions.explanation: The rover's mass is the same everywhere: m = W/g = 1600 N ÷ 10 N/kg = 160 kg. On Mars its weight is 160 kg × 3.7 N/kg = 592 N ≈ 5.9 × 10² N.

questions.stem: A puck slides east at constant velocity across level ice with negligible friction. Starting at time t, a constant force directed north is exerted on the puck, and no other horizontal force acts. Which statement describes the puck's motion after time t?

options.text: It turns and moves due north, in the direction of the force on it.
Its eastward velocity decreases while its northward velocity increases.
It moves at a constant velocity in a direction between east and north.
Its eastward velocity stays the same while its northward velocity increases.

questions.stem: A cylindrical rod is made of a 0.50 m aluminium section joined end to end to a 0.50 m steel section of the same diameter. Each section is uniform, and the steel section has the greater mass. How does the location of the rod's centre of mass compare with the rod's midpoint?

options.text: It is at the midpoint, since the rod's shape is symmetric about that point.
It is on the aluminium side of the midpoint, nearer the lighter section.
It is at the centre of the steel section, the more massive part.
It lies between the midpoint and the centre of the steel section.

questions.stem: A person of mass m stands at one end of a uniform raft of mass 4m and length L. The raft floats at rest on still water, and the water exerts a negligible horizontal force on it. The person walks to the other end of the raft and stops. How far does the raft move relative to the water?
